definition: The system of people, rules and tools that issues and manages digital certificates.
exampleSentence: A public key infrastructure lets every employee device prove its identity safely.

definition: A trusted organization that issues digital certificates after checking identity.
exampleSentence: The browser trusts the website because a known certificate authority signed it.

definition: An electronic document that links a public key to a person or website.
exampleSentence: A digital certificate shows visitors that the website really belongs to our company.

definition: The top-level certificate that all other certificates in a chain depend on.
exampleSentence: Devices must trust our root certificate before they can accept internal websites.

definition: The series of certificates that links a website certificate to a trusted root.
exampleSentence: The error appeared because the certificate chain was missing an intermediate certificate.

definition: Cancelling a certificate before it expires because it is no longer trustworthy.
exampleSentence: After the key leak, we started certificate revocation for all affected servers.

definition: A certificate signed by its owner instead of a trusted authority.
exampleSentence: The browser warned us because the test server used a self-signed certificate.

definition: The standard format used for public key certificates on the internet.
exampleSentence: Each X.509 certificate contains the owner, the public key and an expiry date.

definition: A message sent to a certificate authority to request a signed certificate.
exampleSentence: Generate a CSR on the server and send it to the authority.

definition: A certificate that covers a domain and all of its direct subdomains.
exampleSentence: One wildcard certificate protects every subdomain of our main website.

definition: Making an app accept only a specific known certificate or key.
exampleSentence: Certificate pinning in the mobile app stops attackers from using fake certificates.

definition: The first exchange where a client and server agree on how to encrypt a connection.
exampleSentence: A slow TLS handshake can make a website feel sluggish on mobile networks.

definition: A property that keeps past sessions safe even if a long-term key is stolen later.
exampleSentence: Perfect forward secrecy means old recorded traffic stays unreadable after a key leak.

definition: A set of algorithms that a secure connection uses for key exchange and encryption.
exampleSentence: We disabled every weak cipher suite on the load balancer last month.

definition: A group of protocols that encrypt and authenticate traffic at the network layer.
exampleSentence: The branch office connects to headquarters through an IPsec tunnel.

definition: A modern, fast and simple VPN protocol with a small code base.
exampleSentence: We replaced the old VPN with WireGuard, and connections became faster.

definition: A widely used open-source library for TLS and general cryptography.
exampleSentence: The team updated OpenSSL after the vendor announced a serious security bug.

definition: A free and automated certificate authority.
exampleSentence: We use Let's Encrypt to renew our website certificates automatically every three months.

definition: A tamper-resistant device that stores keys and performs cryptographic operations.
exampleSentence: The bank keeps its signing keys inside an HSM that nobody can copy.

definition: A cloud service for creating, storing and controlling encryption keys.
exampleSentence: The application asks the KMS to decrypt the data instead of storing the key.

definition: Replacing sensitive data with a harmless token that has no real value.
exampleSentence: Tokenization lets us process payments without storing real card numbers.

definition: A slow password hashing algorithm designed to resist brute force attacks.
exampleSentence: We changed the login system to hash passwords with bcrypt.

definition: A modern memory-hard algorithm for hashing passwords securely.
exampleSentence: Argon2 was selected because it makes large-scale password cracking very expensive.

definition: A common hash algorithm that creates a 256-bit fingerprint of data.
exampleSentence: The website publishes the SHA-256 value so you can verify your download.

definition: An old hash algorithm that is no longer safe for security uses.
exampleSentence: Never use MD5 to protect passwords, because it can be broken very quickly.

definition: Algorithms designed to stay secure even against future quantum computers.
exampleSentence: Governments already recommend post-quantum cryptography for data that must stay secret for decades.

definition: A method to prove something is true without revealing the secret itself.
exampleSentence: A zero-knowledge proof lets you show you know a password without sending it.

definition: A shared ledger where records are linked and protected by cryptography.
exampleSentence: Each block in the blockchain contains the hash of the previous block.

definition: A program and standard used to encrypt and sign emails and files.
exampleSentence: Journalists often use PGP to protect messages from their sources.

definition: A standard for signing and encrypting email using certificates.
exampleSentence: The company configured S/MIME so that executives can sign their emails.

definition: An isolated hardware area that protects sensitive keys and operations.
exampleSentence: The phone keeps your fingerprint data in a secure enclave.

definition: Digitally signing software so users can verify its author and integrity.
exampleSentence: Code signing helps users trust that the installer was not modified by anyone.

definition: A collection of trusted root certificates stored on a device or system.
exampleSentence: We added our company root to the trust store of every laptop.

definition: Proving that data existed at a specific time using a trusted authority.
exampleSentence: Trusted timestamping proved that the contract was signed before the deadline.

definition: How well a system or algorithm withstands attempts to guess every possible key.
exampleSentence: Long random keys give excellent brute-force resistance against modern computers.

definition: The ability to switch quickly to new algorithms when old ones become weak.
exampleSentence: Cryptographic agility will make our migration to new algorithms much easier.

definition: Forcing a connection to use an older, weaker protocol or cipher.
exampleSentence: Disabling old protocol versions prevents a downgrade attack on the server.

definition: Public logs that record issued certificates so that mistakes and abuse can be found.
exampleSentence: Certificate transparency helped the security team discover a fake certificate for our domain.

definition: A protocol that checks in real time whether a certificate has been revoked.
exampleSentence: The browser uses OCSP to ask if the website certificate is still valid.

definition: A TLS setup where both client and server prove their identity with certificates.
exampleSentence: Mutual TLS ensures that only approved services can call the payment API.
